text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 15

The panel's composition alone tells you almost nothing. All-female panels are common in many ministries simply because of who holds senior roles there, and panels don't systematically favour their own sex. Raising it as your opening argument makes you look aggrieved rather than credible, and it's the weakest part of your case.

Your stronger ground is procedural: you're entitled to a written explanation and two weeks' silence is unreasonable. Chase that in writing, cite the relevant access-to-information or civil service rules, and ask specifically how the criteria were scored.

If the reasoning reveals that "international project leadership" was weighted in a way not flagged in the advert, you have a real complaint. Build on that, not the panel's sex.
